title: The inclusion of the Zariski site into the small etale site is a morphism of sites
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $X_{\rm Zar}$ its small Zariski site (objects the open subschemes $U\subseteq X$, morphisms the inclusions, coverings the jointly surjective families of open inclusions) [def-sc-zariski-site] and $X_{\Et}$ its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $u:X_{\rm Zar}\to X_{\Et}$ be the functor sending an open subscheme $U$ to the etale $X$-scheme $U\hookrightarrow X$ (an open immersion is etale) and an inclusion $W\subseteq U$ to the corresponding $X$-morphism. Then: (1) $u$ is continuous in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3): a Zariski covering $\{U_i\subseteq U\}$ goes to an etale covering, and for $T\subseteq U$ the canonical morphism $u(T\cap U_i)\to u(T)\times_{u(U)}u(U_i)$ is an isomorphism; (2) $X_{\rm Zar}$ has the final object $X$ and fibre products $V\times_UW=V\cap W$, and $u$ carries $X$ to the final object $\mathrm{id}_X$ of $X_{\Et}$ and commutes with these fibre products; (3) consequently $u_s$ is exact on sheaves of sets, i.e. $u$ defines a morphism of sites $\epsilon:X_{\Et}\to X_{\rm Zar}$ with $\epsilon_*\mathcal F=\mathcal F\circ u$, $(\epsilon_*\mathcal F)(U)=\mathcal F(U\hookrightarrow X)$, and $\epsilon^{-1}=u_s$ its left adjoint.

source.place: Proposition Tag 00X6 (proposition-get-morphism, line 2827), applied to the inclusion functor S_Zar -> S_etale used in etale-cohomology.tex Lemma Tag 09AX (lemma-local-rings-strictly-henselian, line 14212: 'the morphism of sites given by the inclusion functor')

proof.text: *The functor $u$.* For an open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ the inclusion $U\hookrightarrow X$ is an open immersion, hence etale, so it is an object of $X_{\Et}$; for opens $W\subseteq U\subseteq X$ the inclusion $W\hookrightarrow U$ is an $X$-morphism and a morphism of $X_{\Et}$ [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. The morphisms of $X_{\rm Zar}$ [def-sc-zariski-site] are the inclusions $W\subseteq U$, so there is at most one morphism between two objects; $u$ sends $W\subseteq U$ to the inclusion morphism $W\hookrightarrow U$. The inclusion of $U$ in itself goes to $\mathrm{id}_U$ and the composite of the inclusions $V\subseteq W\subseteq U$ goes to the composite $V\hookrightarrow W\hookrightarrow U$, which is the inclusion $V\hookrightarrow U$; so $u:X_{\rm Zar}\to X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] is a functor.

*Finite limits in $X_{\rm Zar}$.* In $X_{\rm Zar}$ [def-sc-zariski-site] every open $U$ has exactly one morphism $U\to X$ (the inclusion $U\subseteq X$), so $X$ is a final object. For morphisms $V\subseteq U\supseteq W$, the open $V\cap W$ with its inclusions into $V$ and $W$ is a fibre product $V\times_UW$: an open $T$ admits morphisms $T\to V$ and $T\to W$ (necessarily compatible over $U$, since there is at most one morphism $T\to U$) iff $T\subseteq V$ and $T\subseteq W$, iff $T\subseteq V\cap W$, and then the morphism $T\to V\cap W$ is unique. In particular for $T\subseteq U$ and $U_i\subseteq U$ one has $T\times_UU_i=T\cap U_i$.

source.place: Proposition Tag 00X6 (proposition-get-morphism, line 2827), hypotheses (1) and (2), checked for $\mathcal C=X_{\rm Zar}$ (written by an agent: 09AX states no verification)

proof.text: *$u$ preserves the final object and fibre products (clause (2)).* By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] (clause 2, for the base $V=X$) $\mathrm{id}_X:X\to X$ is a final object of $X_{\Et}$, and for morphisms $W_1\to W\leftarrow W_2$ of $X_{\Et}$ the scheme-theoretic fibre product $W_1\times_WW_2$, with its map to $X$, is a fibre product in $X_{\Et}$. Hence $u(X)=(X\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}X)$ is final. Let $V,W\subseteq U$ be opens of $X$ and $f:V\to U$ the inclusion. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product], applied to $f$ and the open subscheme $W\subseteq U$, the open subscheme $f^{-1}(W)=V\cap W$ of $V$, with its inclusion into $V$ and the restriction $f|_{V\cap W}:V\cap W\to W$ (the inclusion), is a fibre product $V\times_UW$ of schemes [def-pc-fibre-product]. So the two cones $u(V\cap W)$ (with the inclusions, which are $u$ of the projections of step 2) and $u(V)\times_{u(U)}u(W)$ (the chosen scheme fibre product) are both limit cones of the same diagram of schemes, and the canonical morphism $c:u(V\cap W)\to u(V)\times_{u(U)}u(W)$ (the one compatible with the projections) is an isomorphism of schemes by uniqueness of limits up to unique isomorphism. Both cones lie over $X$ through $U\hookrightarrow X$, so $c$ and $c^{-1}$ are $X$-morphisms, and $c$ is an isomorphism in $X_{\Et}$, whose morphisms are the $X$-morphisms [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Thus $u$ commutes with the fibre products of step 2.

source.place: Lemma Tag 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product, line 3197); topologies.tex Lemma Tag 021D (lemma-fibre-products-etale, line 946)

proof.text: *$u$ is continuous (clause (1)).* Let $\{U_i\subseteq U\}_{i\in I}$ be a covering of $X_{\rm Zar}$, i.e. opens $U_i\subseteq U$ with $\bigcup_iU_i=U$ [def-sc-zariski-site]. (a) Each $u(U_i)\to u(U)$ is the inclusion $U_i\hookrightarrow U$, a morphism of $X_{\Et}$ by step 1, i.e. an etale morphism over $X$; the family is jointly surjective onto $U$ because the $U_i$ cover $U$. So $\{u(U_i)\to u(U)\}_{i\in I}$ is a covering of $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. (b) For a morphism $T\subseteq U$ of $X_{\rm Zar}$, $T\times_UU_i=T\cap U_i$ (step 2) and the canonical morphism $u(T\cap U_i)\to u(T)\times_{u(U)}u(U_i)$ is an isomorphism by step 3 (with $V=T$, $W=U_i$). These are conditions (a) and (b) of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3) (Sites, Definition 00WV), so $u$ is continuous.

*$u_s$ is right exact.* Since $u$ is continuous (step 4), $u^s\mathcal G=\mathcal G\circ u$ is a sheaf of sets on $X_{\rm Zar}$ for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $X_{\Et}$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-continuous-pushforward-sheaf], so by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] $u_s=(u_p-)^\#:\Sh(X_{\rm Zar})\to\Sh(X_{\Et})$ is a left adjoint of $u^s$. A left adjoint carries colimit cocones to colimit cocones [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]; in particular $u_s$ commutes with finite colimits.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00X5 (lemma-directed-morphism, line 2802), first two sentences of the proof, with categories.tex Lemma Tag 0038 (lemma-adjoint-exact)

proof.text: *$u_s$ is left exact.* Write $u_s=\#\circ u_p\circ\iota$, with $\iota:\Sh(X_{\rm Zar})\to\mathrm{PSh}(X_{\rm Zar})$ the inclusion, $u_p:\mathrm{PSh}(X_{\rm Zar})\to\mathrm{PSh}(X_{\Et})$ the presheaf pullback and $\#:\mathrm{PSh}(X_{\Et})\to\Sh(X_{\Et})$ the sheafification, as in [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] (2). (i) $\iota$ commutes with finite limits: a limit of sheaves is the sectionwise limit presheaf, which is also the limit in presheaves [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise] (1). (ii) $u_p$ commutes with finite limits by [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-pullback-sets-left-exact] (2), applied to $b=u$: its hypotheses are that $X_{\rm Zar}$ has a final object and fibre products (step 2) and that $u$ commutes with them (step 3), and that both categories have a set of objects and morphisms (the opens of $X$ form a set; $X_{\Et}$ is taken set-sized, inside a chosen big etale site, as in Stacks Topologies Definition 021B and [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (1)); it also shows that the index categories $\mathcal I_Y^{\rm op}$ of $u_p$ are filtered (Sites, Lemma 00X3). (iii) $\#$ commutes with finite limits [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact]. A composite of functors commuting with finite limits commutes with finite limits, so $u_s$ does.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00X5 (lemma-directed-morphism, line 2802), proof (u_p commutes with finite limits by Categories Lemma 002W since the I_Y^opp are filtered, Lemma 00X3; sheafification commutes with finite limits, Lemma 00WJ; u_s = # o u_p); Proposition Tag 00X6 (proposition-get-morphism, line 2827), proof

proof.text: *Conclusion (clause (3)).* By steps 5 and 6, $u_s$ commutes with finite limits and finite colimits, i.e. it is exact (Categories, Definition 0034). By [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3) (Sites, Definition 00X1) the continuous functor $u$ (step 4) therefore defines a morphism of sites $\epsilon:X_{\Et}\to X_{\rm Zar}$ with $\epsilon_*=u^s$ and $\epsilon^{-1}=u_s$, $\epsilon^{-1}\dashv\epsilon_*$ (step 5), on sheaves of sets and on abelian sheaves; by the definition of $u^s$, $\epsilon_*\mathcal F=\mathcal F\circ u$, i.e. $(\epsilon_*\mathcal F)(U)=\mathcal F(u(U))=\mathcal F(U\hookrightarrow X)$.
